For a retrofit, ask whether the existing hinges, posts and gate construction can work with the proposed operator. Identify any lifting, alterations or temporary removal in the quotation. Include safe access arrangements for residents while the entrance is unavailable.

For replacement equipment, provide the original models and service history. Ask whether existing boxes or parts can be retained and how their condition and compatibility will be established. Do not assume that an operator from the same brand fits the old box or retains every existing control.

At handover, request the care instructions and the documented release arrangements for the exact model. Agree who will inspect drainage and covers during servicing. If the installation develops a fault, describe the symptoms and obtain an assessment before opening concealed equipment.

solar-powered-gate-automation-london.title: Can Solar Power Run a Driveway Gate in London?
solar-powered-gate-automation-london.description: Assess winter generation, shade, standby loads and backup arrangements before choosing solar gate automation.
sections: Start with the complete electrical load

List the motors, controller, intercom, receiver, sensors and any lighting or heaters. Record movement demand and the equipment that remains powered while the gate waits. The number of opening cycles alone cannot determine the required panel and battery.

Use measured consumption or specifications for the exact equipment. Our running-cost calculation separates movement from standby demand.
Design for the site and winter use

Ask the designer to assess panel location, orientation, shading and seasonal generation. Trees, buildings and winter sunlight can change the available energy. An annual generation average does not establish reliable operation through a run of poor weather.

The proposal should state expected use, assumptions for low-generation periods and the battery reserve. Request a site-specific calculation rather than a generic panel, voltage and battery shopping list.
Agree the fallback before ordering

Ask what happens when the battery reaches its operating limit, how you receive a warning and what access remains possible. Confirm charging arrangements, battery replacement and safe manual operation.

A solar supply does not remove the need to assess gate movement, supports or protective measures. The installer must consider the complete powered entrance and how it behaves during a power shortage.
Compare the lifetime scope

Price the solar equipment, mounting, cabling, batteries, maintenance and replacement alongside a suitable mains-supply proposal. Include trenching and reinstatement for the mains option. A payback claim needs those actual costs and load assumptions.

Send the gate location, photographs and expected use when you discuss your entrance. Ask for equipment availability and supported configurations in writing before purchasing a kit.
A small load example with explicit assumptions

The following arithmetic is illustrative, not a recommended system size or a measured London installation. Assume the complete entrance draws 100 watts during movement, operates for 200 seconds per day and draws 5 watts during the remaining time. Movement uses 100 × 200 ÷ 3,600 = 5.56 watt-hours per day. Idle demand uses 5 × (24 − 200 ÷ 3,600) = 119.72 watt-hours. The assumed total is 125.28 watt-hours per day.

That example shows why the designer needs standby demand as well as cycle count. It does not include conversion or charging losses, battery operating limits, additional equipment or a reserve for poor weather. A battery’s nameplate capacity cannot be treated as fully usable energy, and a panel’s rated watts do not state its daily winter output.

Ask for the same calculation using the proposed equipment and site assumptions. Identify which loads the designer has included and how the required reserve was chosen. Keep the calculation with the quotation so a later intercom or lighting addition prompts a review.
Compare solar and mains by project scope

ItemSolar proposalMains proposal
Site workPanel mounting, cables, battery location and access.Supply assessment, cable route, excavation and reinstatement.
Energy planningSeasonal generation, load, storage and low-generation reserve.Suitability of the supply and operating consumption.
Ongoing carePanel and battery care, monitoring and replacement terms.Electrical and gate-system care under the specified instructions.
Interrupted supplyDefined behaviour at low battery and authorised fallback.Defined behaviour during a power cut and any specified backup.

Request comparable gate controls and protective measures in both options. The power-source choice should not quietly remove an access function that the household relies on.
Questions for a solar survey

Show the proposed panel location at different times of day and identify nearby trees or buildings. Ask how the designer will account for seasonal shading and future growth. Confirm whether the mounting position is acceptable for the property and how someone will reach it for maintenance.

Explain normal usage and unusually busy days. Ask what warning the owner receives if energy becomes insufficient and who supports the charging equipment. Do not accept an annual average or a generic payback claim as proof that the gate will operate through the required low-generation period.

smart-gate-integration-ring-nest-control.title: Connecting Driveway Gates to Ring, Nest and Control4
smart-gate-integration-ring-nest-control.description: Compare Ring, Nest and Control4 gate integration: UK product limits, visitor calls, opening commands, gate status, account ownership and fallback access.
sections: Decide what you want the smart-home system to do

You can add smart-home features to some driveway gate installations, but a camera, an opening command and a gate-position signal perform different jobs. Start by listing the actions you need. You might want to answer a delivery driver from your phone, grant access from an indoor screen or check whether the gate has finished closing.

An app showing a successful command does not by itself confirm that the gate moved. A camera view may help you observe the entrance, while a separate status interface may report a position. Ask the installer to identify how the proposed system obtains each piece of information.

Keep the visitor journey in the brief: arrival, calling, answering, authorised entry and departure. That makes it easier to compare a smart-home proposal with a dedicated gate intercom system and to spot a missing function before buying equipment.

Review connected controls alongside the locks, boundary and visitor routine in our guide to driveway and home security.
Ring, Nest and Control4: the practical differences

Platform or productWhat to investigateLimit to resolve
Ring doorbell and Ring IntercomIdentify whether you need a camera or an upgrade to an existing compatible intercom.A doorbell product name does not confirm a gate-release connection.
Ring Access Controller Pro 2A separate access-control product described by Ring.Ring lists this model as supported within the United States; it is not a documented UK solution.
Google Nest doorbellVisitor video and calling alongside the existing entrance system.Google warns that integrated intercom and gate-control systems typically do not work with the doorbell.
Control4A configured door-station, controller and user-interface arrangement.The integrator must specify the supported hardware, software, access command and ongoing service terms.

Use this as a requirements comparison, not a brand ranking. Two installers can propose different functions under the same brand name. Have each quotation state the equipment models and the actions available from each screen or phone.
Ring: distinguish the doorbell, Intercom and access controller

Ring Intercom works with compatible existing intercom systems. The exact model matters, including whether you need audio or video and which entrance the existing system releases. Run the manufacturer’s compatibility check with the correct equipment details and have the installer confirm the complete gate arrangement.

Ring’s Access Controller Pro 2 product information, checked on 13 October 2026, says that the device is supported only within the United States. Its gate-control description should not be read as confirmation of UK availability or support. A Ring support page appearing under a UK web address does not change that limitation.

For a London property, require written confirmation of the proposed UK-supported product and configuration. Do not order an imported access controller on the assumption that an existing Ring camera makes it compatible. If the proposal uses a separate gate app, ask the installer to show that workflow instead of describing it as one integrated Ring experience.
Nest: retain a clear boundary between video and gate release

Google’s Nest doorbell compatibility guidance states that systems with integrated intercoms or front-gate controls typically do not work with the doorbell. A Nest camera or doorbell therefore should not be specified as a direct replacement for an existing gate intercom without checking the arrangement.

You may want a visitor camera while retaining another means of opening the gate. Describe both parts of that setup in the quotation. If a contractor proposes an additional smart controller, request its model, supported interface and manufacturer documentation. Support for a camera in Google Home does not demonstrate support for the separate gate-opening action.

Avoid basing the purchase on promised future compatibility. Have the contractor demonstrate the functions you intend to use with the equipment and software being supplied, including the experience for another household member.
Control4: specify the door station and the programmed actions

Control4’s door-station range provides visitor communication through compatible indoor touchscreens or the Control4 app. Its documentation describes configurable access functions. The integrator still needs to specify the door station, controller, connection to the gate and programmed actions for your installation.

If you already use Control4, give the integrator the existing system details and explain which answering points you want to retain. Ask whether the proposed addition requires other equipment or software changes. Record the remote-access service, licence and support terms that apply to the quoted configuration.

Name each action in plain language, such as vehicle entry or pedestrian access. Avoid an ambiguous button labelled only “gate” if different actions are possible. Agree what information the screen will show after a command and who will correct an integration fault following a later update.
Prepare an equipment and connection checklist

Gather the gate controller details, intercom model and existing system documents. Use paperwork or accessible external labels; do not open electrical enclosures to identify terminals. Photographs from safe positions can show the entrance, current calling point and the route towards the house.

  • Existing controls: list remotes, keypads, indoor monitors and any pedestrian release you want to retain.
  • Connection: identify available cable routes and the network service proposed at each device.
  • Answering points: list the phones and fixed screens that need to receive calls.
  • Gate status: specify whether you need live video, an actual position signal or both.
  • Responsibility: name who will configure the smart-home system and who will assess the gate connection.

The contractor should explain any power, cabling or interface work before quoting a small plug-in module as the whole solution. For a separate phone-entry approach, compare our GSM gate opener guide.
Agree ownership, privacy and recurring charges

Use an owner-controlled account and recovery address where the product supports that arrangement. Decide who receives visitor calls, who may grant access and who can change permissions. A family member needing everyday entry does not necessarily need the same administrative rights as the person maintaining the system.

List subscriptions and support fees beside the functions they fund. Ask what happens if a payment lapses or the owner changes phone. Treat camera recording, cloud storage and remote access as separate requirements until the supplier confirms their terms.

For a shared entrance, agree who removes former residents and manages visitor permissions. If you want recordings, discuss the camera view, storage and access with the responsible person before enabling them. Include removal of the installer’s temporary account access in the handover plan.
Check connection loss and safe remote operation

Work through loss of broadband, a failed phone and loss of power at the gate as separate scenarios. A retained remote may help if the network fails while the gate remains operational. It cannot overcome every electrical or mechanical fault. Ask the contractor to explain fallback access under each condition.

Have the gate engineer assess remote and unattended commands as part of the complete entrance. HSE’s powered-gate guidance explains why competent installation and maintenance matter. Do not bypass protective devices to make an app command work.

During a fault, record which function failed: no visitor notification, a failed conversation, a rejected command or a command followed by no movement. Give that sequence to the responsible installer without resetting accounts or altering wiring. Our access-control options can help you describe the intended arrangement.
Use a handover demonstration to close the gaps

Before accepting the work, walk through the agreed visitor journey with the installer. Include an ordinary household user rather than testing only with the administrator’s phone. Keep people away from moving gates during demonstrations and follow the installer’s instructions.

  1. Call from the entrance and answer at each specified device.
  2. Demonstrate the authorised entry action and explain any displayed status.
  3. Show how to add and remove an everyday user.
  4. Explain which functions remain available during the agreed outage scenarios.
  5. Record models, account ownership, renewals, support contacts and operating instructions.

Keep the demonstrated functions with the quotation and handover records. That gives a future engineer or new owner a clear account of what the integration does and where each service begins and ends.
faqs: Can a Ring doorbell open my driveway gate by itself?
Do not assume so. Visitor video and a compatible gate-release command are separate functions. Identify the exact access product and UK-supported configuration before ordering.
Can Google Nest replace my gate intercom?
Google warns that integrated intercom and gate-control systems typically do not work with Nest doorbells. Ask for a checked arrangement for both visitor communication and gate release.
Does the app tell me that the gate is closed?
Only if the specified system provides suitable status information. A successful opening command or a camera feed alone does not establish a dedicated closed-position signal.

video-intercom-comelit-vs-hikvision.title: Comelit vs Hikvision Gate Intercoms: Compare the Actual System
video-intercom-comelit-vs-hikvision.description: Compare Comelit and Hikvision gate intercom systems: complete kit examples, wiring, phone access, camera checks, ownership costs and installer support.
sections: Compare complete systems for the same entrance

Choose between Comelit and Hikvision by comparing the complete visitor-entry arrangements proposed for your property. Start with the outdoor calling point, indoor answering device, phone access and gate-release connection. A quotation for an outdoor panel alone cannot be compared fairly with a kit that includes a monitor and power equipment.

Write a short brief before collecting prices: one household or several, vehicle gate or pedestrian entrance, fixed screen or phone answering, and recording if needed. Include anyone who cannot rely on a smartphone. Then ask each installer to show how its proposal handles the same visitor journey.

The examples below identify documented equipment combinations. They help you read a quotation or recognise an existing installation; they do not establish current UK stock, a fitted price or compatibility with every gate controller. Request a current supported alternative where an older product has limited availability.
Documented Comelit and Hikvision kit examples

Part of the systemComelit 8451V exampleHikvision DS-KIS603-P(C) example
Outdoor calling pointQuadra 4893M entrance panel.DS-KV6113-WPE1(C) door station.
Indoor answering pointMini Wi-Fi 6741W monitor.DS-KH6320-WTE1 indoor station.
System descriptionSimplebus 2 kit with supported Comelit app functions.IP video intercom kit with Hik-Connect app control.
Buying checkThe reviewed regional listing labels this kit as limited remaining spare stock.Confirm the exact suffix, supplied power equipment and supported firmware.
Gate installationConfirm the release interface and all site work separately.Confirm the release interface and all site work separately.

Comelit’s 8451V kit listing pairs the Quadra panel with the Mini Wi-Fi monitor. On 13 October 2026, that regional listing showed limited spare stock. Treat it as a documented installed-system example and ask a UK supplier about ongoing support or a replacement configuration.

Hikvision’s DS-KIS603-P(C) kit datasheet identifies its outdoor station, indoor station and two power supplies. A product supporting PoE does not establish that a PoE switch comes in every box. Check the quoted contents rather than inferring them from a feature label.

These paired examples correct a common comparison error: the Comelit 6741W is an indoor monitor, while the Hikvision DS-KV6113-WPE1(C) is an outdoor station. Assessing only those two items would compare different roles in the installation.
Existing wiring can change the better option

For a retrofit, ask the installer to record the existing intercom models, cable route and equipment at both ends. A compatible replacement within an established system may reduce disruption, but the contractor still needs to check the condition and suitability of what it intends to retain.

With a proposed IP arrangement, identify the network route, power provision and any required switches or other devices. With a bus-based arrangement, identify the compatible power, panel and monitor combination. Neither a familiar brand nor the number of visible wires proves that old components can remain.

Have each quote distinguish reuse from replacement. Specify who will investigate an undocumented cable and who pays if it cannot be reused. A cheaper panel can lead to a more expensive installed job if it requires a new route through finished paving. Ask for the reinstatement scope before agreeing the work.
Compare the camera and conversation at your gate

Judge a video intercom from the intended calling position. A visitor on foot and a driver sitting in a vehicle may appear at different heights and distances. Tell the installer which matters at your entrance and whether one calling position can serve both.

Request a demonstration or suitable sample view that addresses your conditions: daylight behind the visitor, headlights, darkness and the distance to a face. A resolution figure alone does not tell you whether you will recognise a caller in that setting. Check the view on the actual indoor screen or phone you plan to use.

Listen to a conversation as well as looking at the picture. Explain nearby road noise and any recessed mounting position. Ask how the contractor will check the finished installation and resolve a poor result. Agree the test before ordering so you can distinguish a site problem from an unmet expectation about the product.
Phone answering, indoor screens and missed calls

List the answering devices for each household member. Decide whether you want the indoor monitor and phones to ring together, and what should happen if nobody answers. Have the supplier demonstrate the chosen configuration; app availability does not settle every call-routing question.

Ask which functions need broadband, a cloud service or an active subscription. Separate answering a live visitor, viewing the entrance, reviewing a missed call and storing recordings. Record any limits that matter to you, including supported users or devices, using the exact current product terms.

If you already use a wider smart-home system, include that requirement in the brief before choosing the intercom. Our Ring, Nest and Control4 integration guide explains the separate compatibility checks. Avoid assuming that two products sharing an app-store category can exchange calls or gate commands.
Gate release needs its own installation check

Tell the contractor whether the intercom should request vehicle entry, pedestrian access or release a separate pedestrian lock. Those are different requirements. The proposal should identify the intended action, the gate controller connection and who will configure and check it.

A working video call does not prove that the release connection or the powered gate operates correctly. If an existing intercom rings but fails to open the gate, describe that symptom before buying a replacement panel. An engineer needs to distinguish the calling equipment from the release interface and the gate fault.

Ask the installer to demonstrate the release from each specified answering point and explain what the display confirms. A command acknowledgement is different from verified gate position. Keep the complete gate’s protective measures in place; no intercom brand removes the need to assess the installation.
Compare installed cost and ownership over the same period

Use a written scope rather than an advertised kit price as the basis for the decision. The gate intercom buying guide covers the wider choice of connection methods. For this brand comparison, request matching answering points and functions from both suppliers.

  • Equipment: outdoor station, indoor units, power equipment, mounts, interface components and network devices.
  • Installation: cable investigation, new routes, electrical work, mounting, configuration and reinstatement.
  • Handover: user setup, demonstration, instructions and the agreed checks.
  • Ongoing costs: any subscription, storage, support or maintenance charges, with the functions each covers.
  • Terms: VAT, equipment warranty, workmanship cover, exclusions and charges for a return visit.

If one proposal reuses an existing system and the other replaces it, ask the contractors to explain the difference in scope. You can then decide whether the added function or support arrangement warrants the additional work. There is no useful universal fitted price for every London entrance.
Accounts, updates and support after installation

Agree who owns the administrator account, controls recovery details and can remove a user. For a shared driveway, put those responsibilities with an authorised person who will remain available when residents change. Keep everyday access permissions separate from installation and account-management tasks where the system allows it.

Ask who handles firmware updates and which current equipment they support. An existing CCTV installation from the same manufacturer does not prove that a new intercom will join it in the way you expect. Request confirmation of the particular combined functions, rather than paying for an assumed integration.

If recording forms part of the proposal, agree the camera view, storage location, retention settings and authorised viewers. Record the process for transferring ownership when the property changes hands. Request the supplier’s support contact and what it charges to recover access or reconfigure a replacement phone.
Choose the proposal you can verify

For an existing Comelit installation, investigate a supported compatible upgrade before assuming you need to replace the whole system. For a new or proposed Hikvision IP installation, check the network and complete equipment list alongside the visitor experience. These are starting points for comparison, not a reason to choose either brand without a survey.

Have the chosen contractor demonstrate calling, answering and authorised release, then explain the fallback when a phone or connection is unavailable. Keep the equipment list, written terms and handover records together. Discuss video intercom installation with that brief so the quotation addresses your entrance and the people who use it.
faqs: Is Comelit better than Hikvision for driveway gates?
The complete configuration and installer support matter more than a brand-only ranking. Compare the same answering points, cable work, release function, ownership costs and handover demonstration.
Can I compare a Comelit 6741W with a Hikvision DS-KV6113-WPE1(C)?
They perform different roles: the Comelit item is an indoor monitor and the Hikvision item is an outdoor door station. Compare each complete system with its compatible components.
Can I keep my existing intercom cable?
An installer must check the route, condition and suitability for the proposed equipment. Ask the quotation to identify retained components and the cost implications if they cannot be reused.

article-4-directions-gate-planning-permi.title: Article 4 Directions and Driveway Gate Planning Permission
article-4-directions-gate-planning-permi.description: Check the mapped property and the rights withdrawn by a direction before changing your front boundary.
sections: Read the direction for the address

An Article 4 direction removes specified permitted development rights in a defined area or at specified properties. Its existence somewhere in a borough does not establish the rules for your gate. Obtain the actual direction, map, schedule and effective date from the planning authority.

Check whether the withdrawn rights cover the proposed boundary work. Camden’s Article 4 directory separates different kinds of directions and links to the relevant records; use your own authority’s equivalent.
Check other controls separately

Conservation-area designation, listed status and conditions on earlier planning permissions are separate checks. The position beside a highway and the proposed height can also affect the gate proposal. A neighbour’s replacement gate is not proof that your work is permitted.

Start with the council planning directory and general gate planning guidance. Ask the authority which information it needs for your address.
Prepare a clear enquiry

Provide a site plan, photographs of the existing boundary and a drawing of the proposed gate, pillars and opening direction. Include dimensions, materials and any excavation, paving or access changes.

Ask whether a formal application, consent or certificate is appropriate. Retain the written response and any conditions with the quotation. Set the installation programme after the required checks.
Work through the map and written schedule together

Begin with the council’s official directory, then open the actual direction and its supporting map. Locate your address and the boundary where the work is proposed. Check whether the document applies to the whole property, particular elevations or a mapped area. If the drawing is difficult to interpret, ask the planning team to confirm its application.

Read the schedule of rights withdrawn and compare it with the work you intend to do. A direction relating to a different type of development should not be treated as a blanket prohibition on all changes. Keep the date and document reference so the enquiry refers to the same record the authority uses.
Describe the proposed work in separate parts

Part of the projectDetails to provide
Existing boundaryPhotographs, materials, condition and dimensions.
Gate alteration or replacementProposed height, width, infill, finish and opening direction.
Supports and groundworksPiers, posts, foundations, drainage and excavation.
Automation and controlsVisible equipment, cable routes and associated alterations.
Other access changesPaving, parking layout and any vehicle-crossing proposal.

This makes it easier to obtain advice on the actual project. Avoid describing a complete replacement with new piers as a minor repair, or assuming that a hidden motor means there are no visible or physical changes to consider.
Keep a record before placing the order

Save the applicable direction, map, written advice and any formal decision with the final drawings. Ask the supplier to identify revisions that change the approved or advised scope. Materials, heights and opening arrangements should match the documents used to resolve the permission question.

If you cannot establish whether a right remains available, ask the authority or a qualified planning adviser what formal route can give the required certainty. Do not treat a lack of enforcement against another property as evidence for yours. Resolve the issue before fabrication or removal of existing boundary features.

conservation-area-gate-planning-london.title: Designing Driveway Gates in a Conservation Area
conservation-area-gate-planning-london.description: Use the actual conservation appraisal and property constraints to plan changes to a historic front boundary.
sections: Identify what gives the boundary its character

Photograph the existing gate, railings, piers and adjacent frontage. Note original details you want to retain and damage that needs repair. Find the council’s conservation-area appraisal or management guidance for the actual address.

Avoid assuming that all period homes need the same metalwork, colour or dimensions. A new gate should be discussed in the context of that boundary and the applicable planning controls.
Separate design choices from permission

Check conservation designation, any Article 4 direction, listed status and existing conditions. Demolition or alteration of a boundary can raise a different question from adding automation. Ask the planning authority to identify the process for the complete proposal.

Our Article 4 guide explains how to read a direction. Use the council directory to locate the responsible authority.
Consider repair before replacement

Ask a suitable metalworker or joiner to assess the existing gate and supports. Retaining sound fabric may be an option, but condition and safe operation must guide the proposal. Compare repair, replacement and automation as separate pieces of work.

Our metal-gate restoration guide covers material identification and finish questions. Do not remove historic features before the necessary advice or consent.
Show the complete proposed entrance

Drawings should show gate proportions, infill, pillars, finish and opening path. Include visible controls, cable routes, drainage and groundworks. A concealed motor still needs foundations and maintenance access.

Agree who obtains permissions and which approved details govern fabrication. Compare the quotation against those drawings before ordering.

Further reading: Planning Portal gate and boundary guidance.
Build an address-specific evidence file

Save the council map showing your property, the relevant appraisal and the written controls that apply. Record the document dates and the parts you think relate to the boundary. If a map is unclear, ask the planning team to identify the property before commissioning a design around an assumption.

Include dated photographs from the street and the garden, with close views of hinges, piers, railings and decorative details. Label damage separately from alterations you would like to make. This helps an adviser distinguish a repair proposal from a different frontage design.
Compare repair, adaptation and replacement

A repair brief might retain the leaves and address particular defective joints or fittings. An adaptation might retain the appearance while changing supports or introducing automation. A replacement could alter proportions, materials and the relationship with the adjoining boundary. Describe the actual work instead of relying on the word restoration to cover all three.

Ask the relevant specialist to explain which original parts could remain and which need intervention. Keep that assessment alongside the design drawings. Do not remove a gate for workshop work before the permission question and responsibility for secure temporary access have been resolved.
Prepare a drawing and materials checklist

Show the existing and proposed elevations at a useful scale, together with a plan of the opening path. Label height, width, piers, infill, finials and the adjoining wall or railings. Include the colour, sheen and finish reference, with samples where requested.

Add the position of intercoms, keypads, lights, cabinets and any visible cabling. Show excavation or changes to paving and drainage, even if the finished motor is concealed. Ask the authority or adviser for its current submission requirements rather than assuming this checklist is the complete application.

Before ordering, compare the final quotation and fabrication drawing with any approved details. Keep the decision, conditions and agreed drawing revisions together. If the supplier proposes a change, establish whether it needs further advice before treating it as a harmless substitution.

outward-swinging-gates-uk-rules.title: Can Driveway Gates Open Outwards in London?
outward-swinging-gates-uk-rules.description: Check the highway boundary and the gate’s full movement before choosing an outward-opening layout.
sections: Establish where the highway ends

An outward-opening gate can project beyond the property into a pavement or road. The visible edge of paving does not necessarily establish the legal highway boundary. Show the proposed swept path to the highway authority before choosing the layout.

Section 153 of the Highways Act 1980 addresses doors and gates opening onto a street. Obtain advice on the actual boundary and proposal rather than relying on an invented pavement clearance or fine amount.
Planning and vehicle access are separate checks

Gate height, listed status, withdrawn rights and the boundary work can affect planning requirements. A dropped kerb or vehicle crossing involves a separate highway enquiry. One approval does not settle all those matters.

Use our dropped-kerb guide and council planning directory to prepare the questions.
Compare layouts that fit inside the site

If an inward swing conflicts with a rising driveway or a parked car, ask for a measured comparison with sliding or folding options. Include pedestrians, visitors waiting to enter and manual operation.

See the swing versus sliding guide and sloping-driveway advice. Changing the motor does not resolve a boundary conflict.
Draw the whole swept path against the boundary

Use a plan that distinguishes the gate line, property boundary, highway extent and any shared or third-party land. Show each leaf closed, partway open and fully open. Include handles, stops and other projections rather than drawing only the central line of the leaf.

Mark where a person would stand to use the intercom and where a driver would wait for the gate. Show the usual pedestrian route along the frontage. If a boundary is uncertain, obtain the relevant advice before using the apparent edge of a paving material as the design limit.
Consider a setback as a measured proposal

Setting a gate further inside the property may change where it moves and where vehicles wait. It can also reduce usable parking depth or affect the turning approach. Ask for the full layout to be checked rather than assuming a setback automatically resolves the design.

Compare an inward swing, folding arrangement or sliding option on the same plan. Identify which existing walls, piers or surfaces each alternative would alter. Include the effect on pedestrian entry and on access to bins, meters and garden routes.

For any outward proposal, obtain advice on the actual land and highway position and relevant permissions. Neither a motor selection nor an informal assurance that people rarely walk there settles the question.
Keep permission and fabrication documents aligned

Provide the authority or adviser with existing and proposed plans, dimensions, photographs and an explanation of the work. Include changes to the vehicle crossing and driveway as separate items. Ask which decisions or approvals are needed before work starts.

Once the layout is agreed, compare the supplier’s fabrication drawing with it. Check the opening direction and position of the hinges explicitly. Keep any conditions with the quotation, and ask for further advice if a later change affects the swept path or frontage.

wrought-iron-gate-restoration-london.title: Restoring Metal Driveway Gates in London
wrought-iron-gate-restoration-london.description: Assess the material, structure and finish before choosing repair, repainting, automation or replacement.
sections: Identify the metal and original details

A traditional appearance does not prove a gate is wrought iron. Ask a metalwork specialist to identify the material, previous repairs and the condition of leaves, hinges, fixings and supports. Photograph decorative details before work begins.

A finish can hide loss of section or damaged joints. Separate cosmetic work from structural repair in the assessment, and keep people away from a gate that is unstable.
Agree preparation and repair methods

The proposed method should suit the metal, condition and existing coatings. Ask how the contractor will assess unknown old paint and manage dust, waste and nearby surfaces. Do not start abrasive stripping or heating from a generic restoration recipe.

If the boundary is listed or has conservation controls, check required advice or consent before removing fabric. Read our conservation-area guide and record any conditions in the scope.
Choose a finish for the exterior gate

Compare physical samples for colour, sheen and texture. Ask how the coating system treats joints, edges, repaired areas and the back face. Confirm which preparation and coating stages form part of the quotation.

For a period entrance, compare the gate with the railings, piers and house details. There is no universal heritage-grade finish that replaces an assessment of the actual material and conservation context. Request care instructions and written finish terms.
Assess automation separately

A restored appearance does not establish suitability for powered movement. Ask for assessment of the hinges, supports, geometry, exposure and hazards around the opening before adding a drive.

Compare repair and replacement proposals with equivalent finishing and handover scope. Discuss metal gate options or gate repairs using photographs and your existing service records.
Ask for an assessment-to-handover programme

Start with photographs and an inventory of the gate, matching railings, hinges and decorative pieces. Ask the specialist to separate urgent stability concerns, repairable damage and finish deterioration. Agree whether further findings may emerge after appropriate preparation exposes the material.

The written programme should explain temporary access, removal if needed, transport, workshop or on-site work, finish stages and refitting. Identify who deals with posts, masonry and automation where those fall outside the metalworker’s scope. Record how additional repairs will be priced and authorised.

At completion, compare the work with the inventory and agreed drawings. Ask for the repair record, finish specification and care instructions. For a powered entrance, arrange the relevant gate-system checks after refitting rather than assuming workshop restoration completes the whole job.
Compare finishing proposals by method and result

Proposal detailWhat to ask
PreparationHow will the method suit the identified metal, existing coatings and historic detail?
Coating systemWhich stages and products apply to the exterior gate, repaired areas and fittings?
AppearanceWhat colour, sheen and texture will the approved sample show?
Future repairHow should scratches or local coating failure be assessed and treated?

A finish label does not establish the suitability of the preparation or the quality of a repair beneath it. Ask how the contractor will protect fine detail and deal with inaccessible joints. Keep a sample and written reference so future maintenance has a clear starting point.
Decide what is worth retaining

Compare the significance and condition of the existing metalwork with the alterations required to keep it in service. A gate with useful original detail may justify specialist repair, while extensive loss of structural material may require a different proposal. Ask the specialist to explain the evidence rather than choosing on a photograph of the front face.

Include refitting, support repairs and future care when comparing restoration with replacement. Historic England’s guidance on conserving architectural metals provides background on material-appropriate care. Use professional advice for the actual gate and any conservation controls.

accoya-wood-gates-london.title: Accoya Wood for Driveway Gates
accoya-wood-gates-london.description: Understand modified timber, gate construction, coating care and the difference between material and installation warranties.
sections: What Accoya is

Accoya starts as softwood and undergoes acetylation, a modification process. It is not a naturally occurring hardwood or a chemical-free treatment. Read the manufacturer’s material explanation when comparing it with other timber options.

Specify the actual wood product in the quotation. The appearance of a finished gate also depends on its boards, joints, frame and coating.
Assess the finished gate

Ask how the joiner has designed the gate for its width, weight and movement. Discuss the supports, fittings and exposure alongside the timber choice. Material properties alone cannot guarantee that a complete gate will never move, split or need adjustment.

View a finish sample beside the property. Decide whether you want a painted surface, visible grain or a weathered appearance, and request the care schedule for that choice.
Read each warranty separately

Request the current manufacturer terms for the supplied material and the separate terms for fabrication, finish, fittings, installation and automation. Confirm what a claim covers, exclusions, records required and any labour charges.

A timber warranty does not automatically cover coatings, hinges or the workmanship of a finished gate. Check the documents linked from Accoya’s ownership guidance against the proposed application.
Compare like-for-like alternatives

Use the same dimensions, board layout, finish and automation scope to compare Accoya with other wooden gates. Our timber and aluminium comparison includes wood-effect options. Ask for product availability and written terms before deciding.
Choose the finished appearance and care together

Compare an opaque painted sample, a finish that leaves grain visible and any proposed uncoated or weathering approach with the fabricator. Ask which options are appropriate for its gate construction and the exposure at your entrance. A preference for natural colour should become a written finish brief rather than an assumption that the appearance will remain unchanged.

Look at board ends, joints, the rear face and the transition to hinges and posts. Ask how the finish will be applied to those areas and what happens after cutting or fitting on site. Match the pedestrian gate and adjoining frontage using the same approved samples.

Request the actual cleaning and inspection instructions. Discuss whether you will maintain the finish yourself within those instructions or arrange contractor care. The timber choice does not remove the need to look after fittings or automation.
Separate the promises in a quotation

PartDocument to request
Supplied woodCurrent manufacturer terms for the product and intended application.
Gate constructionFabricator’s terms covering its completed gate and workmanship.
CoatingFinish specification, care requirements and applicable coating terms.
Hinges and installationSupplier and installer terms, including labour and exclusions.
AutomationEquipment and installation terms plus maintenance requirements.

Ask who receives a claim if the cause is unclear. Establish whether removal, transport, refitting or refinishing would be included before treating a material warranty as cover for the complete entrance. Keep proof of the supplied product with the invoice and care records.
Compare an equivalent gate, not just a timber label

Use the same opening dimensions, board arrangement, frame details and controls when requesting an alternative. Ask which changes the fabricator recommends for each timber and why. A price difference may reflect construction, finish or included site work as well as the raw material.

For retained posts or an existing powered entrance, request a suitability assessment of the whole arrangement. A replacement leaf may change weight, geometry or loading. Confirm those interfaces before ordering the new gates and keep the agreed specification for future repairs.

driveway-gates-noise-reduction-london.title: Will Driveway Gates Reduce Traffic Noise?
driveway-gates-noise-reduction-london.description: Consider the complete boundary and the location of the noise before buying gates for acoustic performance.
sections: Do not budget on an untested decibel claim

A gate may change the openness of the front boundary, but its appearance and weight do not establish a particular reduction in traffic noise. Sound can reach the property around and above the entrance, through gaps and by routes unrelated to the gate.

Ask for acoustic evidence that fits the actual proposal before paying for a promised numerical improvement. A result from another property cannot establish the outcome at yours.
Assess the whole frontage

Show an acoustic adviser the road, gate position, adjoining walls, ground levels and the windows or garden area you want to protect. Explain when the disturbance occurs and whether the gate would be open during those periods.

Gate, fence and planting claims cannot simply be added together into a total reduction. Consider the boundary as a whole and compare practical options for the particular source and receiving location.
Check design trade-offs

A closed gate affects views, airflow and wind exposure, and must still provide a suitable entrance for people and vehicles. Ask the gate installer to coordinate any acoustic proposal with the supports, movement and protective measures.

Choose gate materials and layout for the complete entrance. If noise reduction is the main objective, obtain the acoustic assessment before ordering a gate on that promise.

automated-gate-home-insurance.title: Electric Driveway Gates and Home Insurance
automated-gate-home-insurance.description: Ask your insurer how an automated gate affects your policy instead of assuming a premium discount or automatic cover.
sections: Ask about your own policy

There is no insurance discount we can promise for adding a driveway gate. Contact your insurer or broker before relying on the gate as a policy security measure. Describe the proposed installation and any change to property access.

Ask whether you need to notify them when the work is complete and whether the policy contains conditions about operation, locking or maintenance. Request confirmation that you can keep with your policy documents.

When planning changes to the entrance, use our driveway and home security guide to consider gates, vehicle protection and daily access alongside the policy questions.
Clarify what damage and costs are covered

Ask how the policy treats the gate, motors, controls and underground services. Discuss accidental impact, storm or flood damage, electrical faults, wear, theft and the applicable excesses. These are questions for the insurer, not a list of guaranteed cover.

Check whether a damaged gate that blocks the entrance requires a particular claims process before you arrange repairs. A product warranty and an insurance policy cover different risks.
Keep useful records

Retain the quotation, installed product details, invoice, handover information and service records. Take photographs of the completed entrance and record changes to the equipment.

Use our installed gate cost guide to keep the installed scope clear. If you need repair work, agree the inspection charge and authorisation arrangements while checking any insurer requirements.

driveway-gate-property-value-london.title: Do Driveway Gates Add Value to a London Home?
driveway-gate-property-value-london.description: Consider appearance, parking and upkeep without assuming a guaranteed sale-price increase.
sections: Separate enjoyment from resale value

You may want a gate for privacy, appearance or control over access. Those reasons can justify a project without assuming that a buyer will repay its cost. We do not have evidence for a fixed percentage uplift or guaranteed return on a gate installation.

Ask local estate agents or a valuer how the proposed entrance fits the property and its likely buyers. Describe the actual layout, parking space and maintenance requirements rather than asking about gates in general.
Make the entrance work well

A gate should leave suitable room for parking, turning and pedestrian access. Consider visitor calls, deliveries, bins and power cuts. Buyers may ask how easily the entrance works and what it costs to maintain.

Compare designs that suit the frontage and avoid sacrificing usable parking just to fit a preferred opening style. Our layout guide explains the space checks.
Keep the project evidence

Keep the permissions or relevant checks, product information, quotation, handover records and service history. Confirm whether warranties transfer and whether access accounts can be handed to a new owner.

Set the budget around the benefits you want and the installed gate cost guide. Treat any resale estimate as advice about your particular property, not a sales promise attached to the gate.

anthracite-grey-gate-trends-london.title: Choosing Anthracite Grey for Driveway Gates
anthracite-grey-gate-trends-london.description: Compare colour samples, sheen and surrounding materials before specifying an anthracite gate finish.
sections: Use a physical sample

Ask for the proposed coating colour reference, sheen and texture on the actual gate material. A screen image changes with display settings and lighting. Two finishes described as anthracite can look different beside brick, stone or render.

Place a sample outside in sun and shade. Check it beside existing window frames and doors rather than assuming that the same colour name guarantees a visual match.
Specify the complete entrance

Include gate leaves, posts, hinges, visible motor covers and the pedestrian entrance in the finish schedule. Ask which components come from different manufacturers and whether slight variations are expected.

For a wood-effect or two-tone design, inspect the joint between finishes and the rear face. Request a drawing showing the areas to receive each finish.
Compare upkeep and repair options

Ask for cleaning instructions, touch-up advice and written coating terms. Dark colour alone does not establish how much dust will show or how long the finish will last. Avoid choosing on unsourced trend or maintenance percentages.

Compare aluminium and other metal gates using the actual construction and coating specification. Bring your preferred sample when you discuss your entrance.

minimalist-steel-slat-gates-london.title: Steel Slat Driveway Gates: Privacy and Design Choices
minimalist-steel-slat-gates-london.description: Plan slat spacing, sightlines, frame details and safe movement for a contemporary entrance.
sections: View the gaps from more than one angle

Slat width, depth and spacing change how much you can see through the gate. Ask for a sample or drawing showing views from the street, inside the garden and approaching at an angle. A straight-on photograph may hide gaps visible from elsewhere.

Balance privacy with the view needed to leave the driveway. Include the height of a seated driver and pedestrians approaching along the pavement in the design discussion.
Draw the frame and rear face

Confirm the arrangement of frames, slats, joints and fixings on both sides. Ask how the pedestrian gate, posts and adjacent fencing will align. Horizontal and vertical designs can create different visual proportions, but neither orientation alone establishes structural performance.

Discuss any accessible openings or footholds as part of the entrance assessment. Decorative spacing is not a substitute for checking hazards around powered movement.
Specify structure and finish

A closely boarded gate needs assessment for dimensions, exposure, supports and drive requirements. Ask the fabricator to specify the actual metal and corrosion-protection system, including treatment of joints and cut edges.

Compare the proposed finish sample and written maintenance instructions. Explore metal gate options and colour selection before finalising the quotation.

do-i-need-a-dropped-kerb-for-a-driveway-.title: Do You Need a Dropped Kerb for a Driveway Gate?
do-i-need-a-dropped-kerb-for-a-driveway-.description: Check vehicle-crossing approval separately from gate planning, paving and ownership permissions.
sections: A gate does not authorise driving across a pavement

If vehicles will cross a public footway to reach the property, check the vehicle-crossing requirements with the highway authority. An existing opening, gravel drive or gate is not proof that the crossing is approved.

Use the GOV.UK dropped-kerb service to find the relevant council. Ask about an existing crossing as well as a proposed new or widened one.

After confirming the crossing requirements, use our driveway and home security checklist to plan parking positions, pedestrian access and visitor controls within the entrance.
Show the complete access arrangement

Provide photographs, the property address and a plan showing the gate, parking space, road and pavement. Identify street trees, utility covers, lamps and other features near the proposed crossing.

Ask the authority for its current eligibility rules, application process, approved work arrangements and charges. Do not book pavement work on the basis of another borough’s dimensions or a generic online price.
Keep the permissions separate

Check planning requirements for the gate and entrance, highway approval for the crossing, and ownership or lease restrictions. The responsible authority should confirm which processes apply to your address and road.

Paving and drainage need their own design. Read our front-garden paving guide and include approved crossover work and surface reinstatement in the installed gate cost guide.
Existing, new and widened crossings need different enquiries

Your situationInformation to gatherQuestion for the authority
An existing crossing will stayAddress, photographs and any approval or completion records.Does the recorded approval cover the access you intend to use?
You want a new crossingA plan of the road, footway, entrance and proposed parking.Is the location eligible, and what application and work process applies?
You want to widen or move accessExisting and proposed dimensions and nearby street features.What approval is needed for the alteration and associated street work?

Use the answer for your property rather than an assumption based on the neighbour’s driveway. An altered gate line can also affect how vehicles approach an existing crossing, so show the complete proposed layout.
Sequence the crossing and gate projects

Resolve the access proposal before committing to a gate size or finished driveway layout. Ask the highway authority which drawings and supporting information it needs, who may carry out the work and whether other approvals must be obtained first. Keep the written requirements with your project brief.

Then coordinate the permitted crossing, gate position, driveway levels and drainage with the relevant contractors. Identify the work on private land separately from work affecting the highway. Ask who will manage each interface and what happens if an approval requires a different layout.

Avoid promising an installation date until the necessary decisions and work arrangements are known. Fabrication, crossing work and surfacing may follow different programmes. A change to one part of the entrance should prompt a check of the others before materials are ordered.
Prepare a useful first enquiry

Send clear photographs looking from the road towards the parking area and along the pavement in both directions. On the plan, identify trees, lamp columns, utility covers and other features near the proposed access. Explain the vehicle you intend to park and show how it would sit inside the property.

Ask for the current process, charges, eligibility requirements and any survey needed. Keep questions about ownership, leases or shared access separate from the technical crossing design. The council’s response to a highway enquiry does not settle every private right or consent affecting the property.

front-garden-paving-suds-london.title: Front Garden Paving, Drainage and Driveway Gates
front-garden-paving-suds-london.description: Coordinate the paving, water route and gate foundations before changing a front garden entrance.
sections: Check the scope of the paving rules

Planning Portal explains that traditional impermeable front-garden paving over five square metres needs planning permission where water does not run to a permeable area. Its front-garden paving guidance also sets out limits and exceptions to permitted development.

Check property type, listed status, planning conditions and any Article 4 direction before assuming that a permeable surface settles the planning question. Ask the authority about the actual proposal.
Design where the water will go

Tell the contractor about ponding, flooding and the current falls. Ask for the proposed surface build-up, drainage route and maintenance arrangements. A permeable top surface needs a suitable underlying design to work as intended.

Coordinate the paving with gate tracks, motor boxes, supports and cable routes. Avoid setting final paving levels before those details have been agreed.
Treat the vehicle crossing separately

Changing the garden surface does not authorise driving across the public footway. Check the dropped-kerb requirements and any approval for a new or altered crossing.

Ask the quotation to distinguish paving, drainage, gate groundworks and highway work. Record who obtains each permission and who reinstates disturbed surfaces.
Keep the system maintainable

Request cleaning and care instructions for the selected paving and drainage. Identify covers and access points that must remain reachable after the gate is installed.

Consult the government’s permeable-surfacing guidance and use the installed gate cost guide to compare the complete entrance scope.
Compare surface choices with their drainage design

ApproachDesign questionOwnership question
Permeable block pavingWhat sub-base, edge restraint and drainage arrangement suits the site?How should joints and surface permeability be maintained?
Gravel or a stabilised gravel systemHow will the construction support vehicles and meet the gate threshold?How will displaced material be kept away from the gate equipment?
Porous asphalt or another specified permeable surfaceWhat complete construction and discharge route is proposed?What cleaning and repair methods suit the supplied system?
Impermeable paving with designed drainageWhere will runoff go, and which permissions or approvals apply?Who maintains the drainage components and access points?

Compare the proposed build-up, not just the visible finish. Ask the designer to explain any site investigations and how the arrangement deals with existing ground conditions. A product described as permeable is not a complete drainage design.
Coordinate foundations, ducts and final levels

Put the gate installer and driveway contractor’s drawings together before work begins. Agree the positions of supports, tracks where applicable, motor boxes, cable ducts and inspection covers. Mark the finished levels at the opening and along the gate movement path.

Ask who checks these details before concrete, foundations or paving conceal the work. Record responsibility for drainage connections and for restoring disturbed surfaces. A late change in gate position can affect several trades, so resolve it before the driveway finish is laid.

Provide a maintenance access plan for covers and equipment. Avoid placing a decorative border or planter where an engineer needs to stand or remove a cover. Include the pedestrian route and any threshold that somebody must cross with a pushchair or wheelchair.
Handover the whole entrance together

Request the paving specification, drainage information and care instructions alongside the gate documents. Ask how to report ponding or settlement and who investigates an issue at the boundary between the two contractors’ work.

Observe the completed entrance during ordinary wet weather and record unexpected water routes from a safe position. Report them to the responsible contractor rather than altering falls or digging around gate foundations. Keep changes to planting and parking compatible with the agreed drainage and access arrangements.

electric-gate-parcel-delivery-access-lon.title: Parcel and Delivery Access Through Electric Gates
electric-gate-parcel-delivery-access-lon.description: Choose a delivery routine that works when you are home, away or unable to answer an intercom.
sections: Choose where parcels should go

Decide whether a courier should enter the driveway or leave a parcel at an accessible delivery point outside the powered gate. Give clear instructions that do not require climbing, reaching through the gate or leaving goods in its movement path.

Consider pedestrian access and the position of a parcel box before adding an entry device. A delivery routine should also work when you cannot answer a call.

Fit the delivery routine into your wider driveway and home security plan, including side access, vehicle protection and arrangements when nobody can answer.
Manage codes and visitor calls

A keypad can offer temporary or separately managed codes if the selected product supports them. Check how codes expire and how you remove access. Avoid placing a permanent household code in public delivery notes.

A video or phone intercom lets you speak with the visitor, subject to the installed connection and app features. Notifications, recordings and remote release vary by model and account. Request a demonstration rather than assuming they are included.
Keep movement and access separate

Letting a visitor in does not confirm that the gate’s path is clear. The installation needs protective measures for the actual entrance, and users need instructions on where to wait and move. Do not ask a courier to hold a powered leaf open or obstruct a sensor.

Agree an alternative for network or power failure. Keep manual release to trained users following the supplied instructions, rather than sharing a generic release sequence with delivery drivers.
Choose the equipment around the routine
Compare keypad access, video entry and phone entry. Check account ownership and recurring charges in the quotation. Our gate safety guide explains the handover information to request.
Compare delivery routines before buying equipment

RoutineWhat to confirmLimitation to plan for
Parcel point outside the vehicle gateA visible, accessible location that leaves the footway and gate movement clear.Parcel size, collection and the courier’s ability to use it.
Resident answers an intercomWhere the call arrives and how entry and exit are managed.Nobody answers, or the connection fails.
Temporary code where supportedWho creates it, when it expires and which entrance it operates.An expired or forwarded code and a driver needing assistance.
Agreed staffed delivery windowWho receives the delivery and supervises the agreed access routine.A vehicle arriving early, late or at the wrong entrance.

Choose the fallback at the same time as the preferred routine. A new control adds little convenience if every missed call still leaves a driver unable to reach an agreed delivery point.
Write instructions a first-time courier can follow

Describe the correct entrance, where to wait and how to call the recipient. Include a recognisable house number or entrance name rather than relying on a driver seeing an app map at exactly the right scale. Keep instructions short enough to follow without entering the gate path.

State what to do if nobody answers. That might be a specified parcel point or the carrier’s normal failed-delivery process. Do not invite a driver to climb over, reach through, defeat a latch or follow another vehicle inside. Check the carrier’s own delivery options rather than assuming it accepts every arrangement.

For bulky items, agree access with the supplier before the delivery day. Confirm the vehicle and handling space, and explain any restrictions. A routine suitable for a small parcel may be unsuitable for a pallet or a long vehicle.
Test the routine with the household

Walk through the plan with the installer and the people who receive calls. Include someone using a normal resident account instead of only the administrator’s phone. Ask how temporary permissions are removed and how to contact support if a delivery code does not work.

Review the routine after a phone change, new tenant or change in work hours. Keep the parcel point and signs usable as planting grows or bins move. The aim is a repeatable delivery process that does not depend on improvising around a powered gate.

electric-sliding-gates.title: Electric Sliding Gates
electric-sliding-gates.description: Electric sliding gates designed around your London driveway, side space, supports and access requirements.
sections: Why choose a sliding gate?

A pair of swing gates on a 3.5-metre opening needs roughly 2 metres of clear drive behind it for the leaves to open. On many London frontages, that space is where the car parks. A sliding gate needs almost no depth. You can park right up to it and it still opens. Sliding gates also cope with drives that slope up from the road. The gate travels across the entrance rather than swinging into the slope, so what matters is the ground along the gate line, not the gradient of the drive. They’re also less affected by wind than a pair of long swing leaves, and generally more secure, because there’s no centre joint to force.

The trade-off is side space. The gate needs somewhere to go when it’s open.
Tracked, cantilever or telescopic

Tracked gates run on wheels along a steel rail across the entrance. They need side space roughly equal to the opening plus a few hundred millimetres for the motor and end post. For a 3.5-metre opening, allow about 4 metres of straight, clear fence line or wall. They’re the most economical sliding gate and suit most London homes. The track has to be kept clear of leaves and grit, and needs drainage so water doesn’t pool against it. They’re a poor fit for gravel drives, because stones get into the track.

Cantilever gates hang from rollers fixed to a foundation beside the opening, so nothing touches the ground across the entrance. They give a clean threshold that works with gravel, block paving or resin, and there’s no track to clean or freeze. In return, they need more side space, because the gate carries a counterbalancing tail, typically adding 40 to 50 percent to the gate’s length. A 3.5-metre opening needs around 5 metres of run. Our heavy-duty sliding gates page covers larger cantilever gates for commercial sites.

Telescopic gates are made of two or more panels that slide over each other, so the open gate takes up roughly half the side space. They’re the answer when your boundary turns a corner or meets the house close to the entrance. They need a little more depth, because the panels sit side by side when open, and they cost more than a single-panel gate.
Checking the side space

The run-back area is the strip behind your fence or wall where the open gate sits. It needs to be straight, roughly level along its length, and clear of obstructions. Common problems on London properties are downpipes and gas meters on the side of the house, steps and doorways, trees and roots, inspection chambers and a neighbour’s fence that isn’t straight. We measure all of this at survey and give you a drawing showing the clear opening, where the gate sits when open, and the foundations.
Safety in the run-back area

A sliding gate can trap someone in two places: at the closing edge, where it meets the end post, and in the run-back area, where a person or child could be caught between the moving gate and a wall or fence. We fit photocells across the opening and safety edges on the gate’s leading and trailing edges. Where the gate runs close to a fence, wall or open area, the run-back is guarded with mesh or a fixed panel so nobody can get between them. Closing forces are tested and recorded against BS EN 12453 at handover. You’ll also be shown how to release the gate by hand. See our manual release guide.
Motors and features

Residential sliding gates use a motor mounted on a plinth inside the boundary, driving a toothed rack fixed along the gate. 24V motors are the usual recommendation for homes. They slow the gate gently at each end, detect obstructions precisely and can run on battery backup in a power cut. Light aluminium gates can use a nylon rack, while heavier steel and timber gates need a galvanised steel rack.

A typical domestic sliding gate opens at around 15 to 25 centimetres per second, so a 4-metre gate takes roughly 20 seconds to open fully. A part-open setting for people on foot is worth having. It opens the gate about a metre so you can walk through without waiting for the full opening. Sliding gates work with every type of access control: video intercoms, keypads, GSM phone entry and ANPR.
Gate material and finish

Aluminium is the most popular material for sliding gates. It’s light, so it’s easy on the motor and rollers, it doesn’t rust, and it comes in slatted, solid and wood-effect designs. See aluminium driveway gates. Steel suits traditional bar designs and should be galvanised and powder-coated. Timber and composite sliding gates are built on a steel or aluminium frame to keep them rigid. Fully solid gates catch the wind, so they need a correctly sized motor and well-fixed guide rollers. A matching pedestrian gate completes the frontage.
Installation

Tracked gates need a concrete strip across the opening for the track, and a plinth for the motor. Cantilever gates need a reinforced foundation along the run-back to carry the rollers. We lay ducting for power and control cables at the same time, and cut and reinstate paving or tarmac around the work. Tracked gates are usually installed in two to three days. Cantilever gates are installed in two visits about a week apart, so the foundation can cure before the gate is hung. If you’re resurfacing the drive, tell us early. It’s much cheaper to put foundations and ducts in before the new surface goes down.
Cost of electric sliding gates in London

As a rough guide, a tracked electric sliding gate for a typical 3.5 to 4-metre residential opening costs £5,000 to £9,000 supplied and fitted with motor and basic controls. Cantilever gates usually cost £7,000 to £12,000, and telescopic gates £8,000 to £13,000. Automating an existing sliding gate is typically £2,000 to £3,500. Intercoms, extensive groundworks and drive reinstatement are itemised separately. See our installed gate cost guide for more.
Looking after a sliding gate

Have the gate serviced once a year. A service covers checking the motor, rack, rollers and safety devices, testing the closing force and testing the battery backup. In between, keep the track clear of leaves and stones, keep the photocell lenses clean, and don’t let plants grow into the run-back area. See gate repair and servicing if the gate starts sticking or reversing.

faqs.question: How much side space does a sliding gate need?
faqs.answer: For a tracked gate, roughly the width of the opening plus a few hundred millimetres. For a cantilever gate, about one and a half times the opening. A telescopic gate needs about half the opening plus the overlap. We measure it precisely at survey.

faqs.question: Can a sliding gate work on a sloping drive?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. A drive that slopes up from the road is often the reason people choose a sliding gate. What needs to be level is the ground along the gate line and the run-back, not the drive itself. A gate sliding along a slope needs a stepped or raked design and careful engineering.

faqs.question: Swing or sliding?
faqs.answer: Sliding if your drive is short, you park close to the gate, or the drive rises behind it. Swing if you lack side space or want the lower cost. Our swing vs sliding guide compares them, and electric swing gates covers the alternative.

faqs.question: Will a tracked gate work on a gravel drive?
faqs.answer: Not well, because stones get into the track and jam the wheels. A cantilever gate is the better choice on gravel.

faqs.question: How long will installation take?
faqs.answer: Two to three days for most tracked gates. Cantilever gates take two visits about a week apart. Larger groundworks or new power supplies add time.

faqs.question: Do I need planning permission?
faqs.answer: Gates next to a road or footpath can usually be up to 1 metre high under permitted development rules. Taller gates, conservation areas and listed buildings need checking. See our borough planning guides.

electric-swing-gates.title: Electric Swing Gates
electric-swing-gates.description: Single and paired electric swing gates planned around your opening, parking space and everyday access.
sections: How much space do you need?

A swing gate needs clear space for each leaf to open fully, plus a margin. For a typical 3.5-metre opening with a pair of gates, each leaf is about 1.75 metres long. That means a clear arc of roughly 2 metres behind the gate line, with no parked car, bin, step or planter in the way. Your car also has to stop outside the arc while the gates open, or wait on the road if it can’t. On a short London front drive, that is often what decides between swing and sliding.

A pair of gates halves the arc each leaf needs, so it’s the usual choice on driveways. A single leaf works well for narrower openings up to about 3 metres, or where one side of the drive is blocked by a wall, tree or step. For a comfortable entrance from a narrow road, aim for an opening of at least 3.5 to 4 metres. Turning in from a tight street with parked cars opposite needs more width than driving straight in.

If space behind the gate is tight, a sliding gate or bi-folding swing gate may be the better answer. Our swing vs sliding guide compares the layouts.
Sloping driveways

A drive that rises behind the gate is the most common problem with swing gates, because the bottom of the leaf hits the ground partway through its swing. There are a few ways round it. The gate can be made with a raked or stepped bottom rail that follows the slope. It can be hung higher, leaving a larger gap under it when closed. It can open outwards, if that’s permitted (see below). Or you can switch to a sliding gate. Fitting a more powerful motor doesn’t solve a slope problem. A drive that falls away behind the gate is much less of an issue. Our guide to automated gates on sloping driveways goes into more detail.
Can the gates open outwards?

Not over a public pavement or road. Section 153 of the Highways Act 1980 lets the council require any gate that opens outward onto a highway to be altered, and a gate swinging into pedestrians or traffic is a real hazard. Outward opening is only an option where there’s private land, such as a private drive or a deep verge you own, between the gate and the pavement. Our outward-opening gate guide explains the rules, and your borough’s planning guide covers gate height and conservation area limits.
Choosing the motor

Ram motors are mounted on the inside face of the gate and pier. They’re the most common and most economical option, suit most residential gates, and are easy to service. They need a modest amount of space between the hinge and the inside edge of the pier, which most London piers have.

Articulated arm motors have a folding arm, like a door closer. They suit deep brick piers where the hinge is set well back from the inside face and a ram won’t fit. They can also open gates past 90 degrees.

Underground motors sit in a steel box buried under each hinge, so nothing is visible above ground. They’re the choice for period homes, ornamental ironwork and anyone who wants a completely clean look. They cost more to install, and the foundation boxes must drain properly, usually to a soakaway or drain, because a flooded box will eventually kill the motor.

There’s also the question of power. 24V low-voltage motors are now the standard recommendation for homes. They slow down gently at each end of the travel, sense obstructions precisely, and can run on battery backup during a power cut. Mains-powered (230V) motors and hydraulic motors are tougher for very heavy gates and high-use entrances. We use established brands such as BFT, CAME, FAAC and Nice, chosen to suit the gate’s weight, length and wind exposure.
Safety

Every automated gate has to be safe for the people around it, including children, visitors and delivery drivers who’ve never seen it before. We fit photocells across the opening and, where needed, safety edges on the leading edge of each leaf. We check the gap at the hinge side where fingers could be trapped, and the space between the open leaf and any wall, where someone could be crushed. Closing forces are tested and recorded against BS EN 12453 at handover. Then we show you how to release the gates by hand. Our manual release guide covers the common systems.
Wind and locking

Solid boarded gates catch the wind like a sail, which strains the motors and can push the gates open. Long leaves, solid infill and exposed sites benefit from a central ground stop for the leaves to close against, and an electric lock that holds them shut. Both reduce the load on the motors and improve security.
Power and cabling

Your gates need a dedicated electrical supply, run from your consumer unit to the control panel by the gate, with an isolator switch nearby. The cable between the two leaves runs in a duct under the drive. If you’re having the drive relaid, put the ducting in at the same time and save digging later. Access control, such as an intercom, keypad, GSM phone entry or ANPR, is planned with the cabling.
Cost of electric swing gates in London

As a rough guide, automating an existing pair of swing gates with ram motors typically costs £2,500 to £4,500 installed. Articulated arm motors are similar to slightly more. Underground motors usually run £4,000 to £7,000. A complete installation with new gates, motors and access control generally costs £5,000 to £12,000 or more, depending on the gate material and design. Groundworks, new piers and intercoms are itemised separately. See our installed gate cost guide for more.
